slides.text:
A function can be defined inside the body of another one. It is a normal function with a name, parameters and a return value, but it exists only inside the function that holds it.

Pseudo code, not Rust.
Use it for a small helper that only one function needs, so the rest of the file never sees it. This module covers how to define one, how helpers call each other and what a nested function can reach.

exercises.title: A helper inside main
exercises.guide: Put a function that adds 10% tax inside `main`, then call it twice.

chunks.guide: Define the helper inside the body of `main`, like any function.

notes.text: Only main can call this function.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Look at where `area` is called and where it is defined.
exercises.explanation: A nested function belongs to the whole body it sits in, so it can be called above its definition. Unlike a `let`, it does not wait for its line.

exercises.title: Helpers using helpers
exercises.guide: Write two helpers in `main`: one squares a number, the other calls it to build a squared distance.

chunks.guide: The first helper squares a number.
The second helper adds two squares.

notes.text: A nested function can call its sibling helpers.

chunks.guide: A step of 3 east and 4 north.

exercises.title: Reuse a helper
exercises.guide: Make the volume helper reuse the area helper, then print the volume of a 2 by 3 by 4 box.

exercises.title: Why inside main?
exercises.guide: Pick the real reason to write `cap` inside `main`.
options: It makes `cap` run faster than a normal one
It lets `cap` read the variables of `main`
It keeps `cap` next to its only caller
It lets other functions in the file call `cap`
exercises.explanation: A nested function is private to the function around it. It is a way to keep a small helper close to the one place that uses it.

slides.text:
A nested function can see other functions and constants of the body around it. It cannot see the `let` variables of that body, so any value it needs must come in as a parameter.

Pseudo code, not Rust.
Names follow the braces. A nested function lives in the block where it is written, and a nested function in an inner block can reuse a name from an outer one.

exercises.title: Pass the value in
exercises.guide: Compute a fee from a rate. The helper cannot see the rate in `main`, so it receives it as a parameter.

chunks.guide: The helper takes the amount and the rate. It has no way to read `rate` from `main`.

notes.text: The rate arrives here, since main's rate is out of reach.

chunks.text:
println!("fee: {}", fee(250, rate));
    println!("fee: {}", fee(1000, rate));

exercises.title: Which limit counts?
exercises.guide: `over` has its own `limit` parameter, and `main` has a `limit` variable. Follow the value the call hands over.
exercises.explanation: The helper cannot see the `limit` of `main`. It only knows the value it receives, 150, and 120 is not over 150.

exercises.title: Center with a constant
exercises.guide: A `const` is the one kind of value a nested function can read directly. Center a label in a 40 column line.

chunks.guide: A constant of the line width, declared in `main`.
The helper computes the padding on the left.

notes.text: Reads the const directly, no parameter needed.

chunks.guide: Padding for a label of 10 characters and one of 24.

exercises.title: Constant and argument
exercises.guide: Cap the score at the limit. Read the constant inside the helper and hand over the variable at the call.

exercises.title: Same name, inner block
exercises.guide: Define a helper, then define another with the same name inside a block. Print before, inside and after.

chunks.guide: A helper that returns a tax rate, printed.
In a block, define a new `tax_rate`. Inside the block, it is the one that counts.

notes.text: A new helper that exists only inside this block.

chunks.guide: Back outside the block, the first one is the one in view again.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: The two helpers call each other. Follow each call down to zero.
options: Nothing, `is_odd` is used before its definition
exercises.explanation: Sibling helpers can call each other in any order. `is_even(4)` ends at `is_even(0)`, which is true, and `is_odd(3)` also ends at `is_even(0)`: true true.
